context: Dealership network that sells, rents and services material handling, construction and environmental processing equipment.

Sum (31.3).

workingCapitalIncrease.note: Includes the rent-to-sell proceeds line, which the company places in working capital. Excluding it, the increase would be 129.5.

depreciation.note: Includes 13.6 of depreciation on inventory rented under purchase-option leases.

rentalCapex.note: Informational. Understates fleet reinvestment: 100.0 moved from inventory to rental fleet as a non-cash transfer.

manual.cite: 10-K Item 1: 'We have operated as an equipment dealership for 41 years'.

maintenanceCapex.estimate: Depreciation ($123.3M rental and non-rental) used as maintenance capex proxy, scaled with revenue in stress.

caveats: JUDGMENT, floorplan: $313.3M of floorplan is left out of debt. $47.7M of it is a JPMorgan first-lien facility that shares collateral with the ABL and could be treated as funded debt.
ESTIMATE, debt service: uses non-floorplan interest expense ($77.5M), not cash. It includes $5.4M of non-cash amortization and undisclosed used and rental floorplan interest.
JUDGMENT, liquidity: the $424.4M available is combined ABL and floorplan capacity. Floorplan capacity can only fund inventory, so this overstates general liquidity.
NOTE, stockholders equity is negative ($8.8M) at year end.

expected.reason: A 60-month loan runs into 2029, when the ABL and second lien notes mature. That is the concern.

discussion: Claude's read, Joel to confirm. Acceptable (FAIL vs Joel's FLAG). Tranche fails on cash flow: after fleet capex and working capital, free cash flow is negative (cash-flow DSCR -0.14x), and leverage is 5.3x. Joel's concern, $714M of ABL and notes maturing in 2029 inside the loan term, is not something Tranche sees (P1-21). Same verdict family, different reasons.
